questions.question: Rahul’s age is three times the age of his daughter. After 8 years from now, his age will be 5 years more than twice the age of his daughter. Find the present age of Rahul.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Rahul's age be 3 units and his daughter's age be 1 unit.

After 8 years, Rahul's age is 2 times her age plus 5 years.

Equating directly: 3 units + 8 = 2 × (1 unit + 8) + 5

3 units + 8 = 2 units + 21 ⇒ 1 unit = 13

Rahul's present age = 3 units = 3 × 13 = 39 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 39 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ After 8 years, his age will be 5 years more than twice the age of his daughter.

 Condition: 3x + 8 = 2(x + 8) + 5

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the present age of the daughter be x years.

⇒ Present age of Rahul = 3x

⇒ Age of daughter after 8 years = x + 8

⇒ Age of Rahul after 8 years = 3x + 8

⇒ According to the condition: 3x + 8 = 2 × (x + 8) + 5

⇒ 3x + 8 = 2x + 16 + 5

⇒ 3x + 8 = 2x + 21

⇒ 3x − 2x = 21 − 8

⇒ x = 13

⇒ Daughter's present age = 13 years

⇒ Rahul's present age = 3x = 3 × 13 = 39 years

**∴ The correct answer is 39 years.**

questions.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point on the ground, which is 48m away from the foot of the tower is 30°. Find the height of the tower.

Side opposite to **60°** (Base) = 48 m.

√3 units = 48 m ⇒ 1 unit = 48/√3 m.

Height (side opposite to 30°) = 1 unit = 16√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 16√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ tan 30° = h / 48

⇒ 1/√3 = h / 48

⇒ h = 48 / √3

⇒ h = (48 × √3) / (√3 × √3)

⇒ h = 48√3 / 3 = 16√3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 16√3 m.**

questions.question: Arvind is now 40 years old and Asha is 25 years old. How many years ago from now was Arvind four times as old as Asha?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Age difference between **Arvind** and **Asha** is always constant: 40 − 25 = **15 years**.

When **Arvind** was **4 times** as old as **Asha**, the ratio was 4 : 1.

Difference in ratio parts = 4 − 1 = 3 units.

3 units = 15 years ⇒ 1 unit = 5 years (Asha's age then).

Years ago = Current age − Past age = 25 − 5 = **20 years**.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Current age of **Arvind** = 40 years, Current age of **Asha** = 25 years.

**Formula Used:** (Current Age − x) = Ratio × (Other Current Age − x)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed71a2f0d776a03b4d05cee31b9767db7e5f9de0ae954cecd4ec63311cc49053.png] 

Let **x** be the number of years ago.

⇒ (40 − x) = 4 × (25 − x)

⇒ 40 − x = 100 − 4x

⇒ 4x − x = 100 − 40

⇒ 3x = 60

⇒ x = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The numerical difference between the ages of two persons remains the same throughout their lives, regardless of the years passed or ratio changes.

Ratio Adjustment Method

If the age ratio is given for two different time periods, multiply the ratios so that the difference between the ratio parts of the two people is equalized.

Future/Past Calculation

To find age 'n' years ago, subtract 'n' from present age. To find age 'n' years hence, add 'n' to present age.</p

questions.question: If tan theta = (7)/(8) , then evaluate ((1 + sin theta)(1 - sin theta))/((1 + cos theta)(1 - cos theta)(cot theta))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simplify the expression using **trigonometric identities**: (1 + sin θ)(1 − sin θ) = cos² θ and (1 + cos θ)(1 − cos θ) = sin² θ.

The expression becomes (cos² θ) ÷ (sin² θ × cot θ).

Since cos² θ ÷ sin² θ = cot² θ, the expression simplifies to cot² θ ÷ cot θ = **cot θ**.

Given tan θ = 7/8, then cot θ = 1 ÷ tan θ = 8/7.

**∴ The correct answer is 8/7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** tan θ = 7/8

**Formula Used:** (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²; sin² θ + cos² θ = 1; cot θ = cos θ / sin θ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a28bea436aad6a8556097a30cc92e71124b740bd27808d0a23d4dc6da9cbf23b.png] 

⇒ Expression = [(1 + sin θ)(1 − sin θ)] ÷ [(1 + cos θ)(1 − cos θ)(cot θ)]

⇒ Using (a+b)(a-b) ⇒ (1 − sin² θ) ÷ [(1 − cos² θ) × cot θ]

⇒ Using identities ⇒ cos² θ ÷ (sin² θ × cot θ)

⇒ (cos² θ / sin² θ) × (1 / cot θ)

⇒ cot² θ × (1 / cot θ) = cot θ

⇒ cot θ = 1 / tan θ = 1 / (7/8) = 8/7

**∴ The correct answer is 8/7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Reciprocal Identities

tan θ = 1/cot θ, sin θ = 1/cosec θ, and cos θ = 1/sec θ.

Pythagorean Identities

sin² θ + cos² θ = 1; 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ; 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.

Quotient Identities

tan θ = sin θ / cos θ and cot θ = cos θ / sin θ.</p

questions.question: The ratio of the age of a son after 15 years and the present age of his father is 2 : 3. 5 years ago, the age of the father was 4 times the age of the son. The present ages (in years) of the father and the son, respectively, are:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the options against the condition: 5 years ago, **Father** was 4 times **Son**.

Option (1) 32, 8 → 5 yrs ago: 27, 3 (9 times) ×

Option (2) 50, 20 → 5 yrs ago: 45, 15 (3 times) ×

Option (3) 45, 15 → 5 yrs ago: 40, 10 (4 times) ✓

Second condition check: (15+15) : 45 = 30 : 45 = 2 : 3 ✓

**∴ The correct answer is 45:15 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4718b08a96dc566197cc53e3514e36f14bb74ca6b39f6b27d29b9b202393ec11.png] 

**Given:** Ratio after 15 yrs (Son) to Present (Father) = 2 : 3. Ratio 5 yrs ago F : S = 4 : 1.

⇒ Let ages 5 years ago be **Father** = 4x and **Son** = x.

⇒ Present age of **Father** = 4x + 5 and **Son** = x + 5.

⇒ **Son's** age after 15 years = (x + 5) + 15 = x + 20.

⇒ According to question: (x + 20) / (4x + 5) = 2 / 3

⇒ 3(x + 20) = 2(4x + 5)

⇒ 3x + 60 = 8x + 10

⇒ 5x = 50 ⇒ x = 10.

⇒ Present **Father** = 4(10) + 5 = 45 years.

⇒ Present **Son** = 10 + 5 = 15 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 45:15 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Age Ratio Constant Difference

The numerical difference between the ages of two persons always remains constant regardless of the number of years passed.

Present Age Conversion

If age 'n' years ago is x, present age is x + n. If age after 'n' years is y, present age is y − n.</p

questions.question: If cot θ = 3/4, then find the value of sin 3θ.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given **cot θ = 3/4** (Base/Perpendicular), so **sin θ = 4/5**.

Apply direct formula: **sin 3θ = 3 sin θ − 4 sin³θ**.

⇒ sin 3θ = 3(4/5) − 4(4/5)³ = 12/5 − 256/125.

⇒ (300 − 256)/125 = 44/125.

**∴ The correct answer is 44/125.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/18f71c13e04c56bf9d2dbfb40328ba929e848c447b177c851f5329a2d9302547.png] 

**Given:** cot θ = 3/4

**Formula Used:** sin 3θ = 3 sin θ − 4 sin³θ

⇒ In a right-angled triangle, if **cot θ = Base/Perpendicular = 3/4**,

⇒ **Hypotenuse (H)** = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = 5.

⇒ **sin θ** = Perpendicular/Hypotenuse = 4/5.

⇒ **sin 3θ** = 3(4/5) − 4(4/5)³

⇒ sin 3θ = 12/5 − 4(64/125)

⇒ sin 3θ = 12/5 − 256/125

⇒ sin 3θ = (12 × 25 − 256) / 125

⇒ sin 3θ = (300 − 256) / 125 = 44/125.

**∴ The correct answer is 44/125.**

**__Additional Information__**

Multiple Angle Formulas

cos 3θ = 4 cos³θ − 3 cos θ and tan 3θ = (3 tan θ − tan³θ) / (1 − 3 tan²θ).

Pythagorean Triplet

The numbers (3, 4, 5) form a **Pythagorean triplet** where 3² + 4² = 5².

Trigonometric Ratios

sin θ = 1/cosec θ, cos θ = 1/sec θ, and tan θ = 1/cot θ.</p

questions.question: If 3 times the mother's present age is 36 years more than 5 times her daughter's age, and 3 times the daughter's age is 4 years less than the mother's age, then what is the difference (in years) between the present ages of the mother and the daughter?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Mother** = M and **Daughter** = D.

From 2nd condition: M − 3D = 4 ⇒ M = 3D + 4.

Substitute in 1st condition: 3(3D + 4) = 5D + 36 ⇒ 9D + 12 = 5D + 36.

4D = 24 ⇒ D = 6 years and M = 3(6) + 4 = 22 years.

Difference = 22 − 6 = 16 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/29e279f8d7a527718e734272dc125de8b97dbaa88ff02e795e2f79608f10964c.png] 

**Given:**

Condition 1: 3 × **Mother's age** = 5 × **Daughter's age** + 36

Condition 2: 3 × **Daughter's age** = **Mother's age** − 4

⇒ 3M − 5D = 36 ... (i)

⇒ M − 3D = 4 ... (ii)

Multiply equation (ii) by 3:

⇒ 3M − 9D = 12 ... (iii)

Subtract (iii) from (i):

⇒ (3M − 5D) − (3M − 9D) = 36 − 12

⇒ 4D = 24

⇒ D = 6 years

Substitute D = 6 in (ii):

⇒ M − 3(6) = 4

⇒ M − 18 = 4

⇒ M = 22 years

**Age Difference** = M − D = 22 − 6 = 16 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

Problems involving two people's ages often lead to a system of two equations that can be solved using **substitution** or **elimination** methods.

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two individuals remains **constant** regardless of how many years pass or go back in time.

Ratio of Ages

If the ratio of ages is given as a:b, we can assume the ages as **ax** and **bx** to simplify algebraic calculations.</p

questions.question: The value of 3 + tan² θ + cot² θ − sec² θ cosec² θ is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put **θ = 45°** directly into the expression.

⇒ 3 + tan² 45° + cot² 45° − sec² 45° cosec² 45°

⇒ 3 + 1² + 1² − (√2)² × (√2)²

⇒ 3 + 1 + 1 − 2 × 2 = 5 − 4 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 3 + tan² θ + cot² θ − sec² θ cosec² θ

**Formula Used:**

1 + tan² θ = sec² θ

1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ

sec² θ cosec² θ = sec² θ + cosec² θ

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3 + tan² θ + cot² θ − sec² θ cosec² θ

We can rewrite 3 as 1 + 1 + 1:

⇒ 1 + (1 + tan² θ) + (1 + cot² θ) − sec² θ cosec² θ

⇒ 1 + sec² θ + cosec² θ − sec² θ cosec² θ

Since sec² θ cosec² θ = sec² θ + cosec² θ:

⇒ 1 + (sec² θ + cosec² θ) − (sec² θ + cosec² θ)

⇒ 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

The three fundamental Pythagorean identities are sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ, and 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.

Product to Sum Identity

The identity sec² θ cosec² θ = sec² θ + cosec² θ is extremely useful for simplifying complex trigonometric algebraic expressions.</p

questions.question: The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 19 years more than 2 times the present age of the son. After 15 years, 12 times the father's age will be 17 years less than 13 times the son's age. The difference (in years) between the present ages of the father and the son is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the first condition: **Father** + **Son** = 2 × **Son** + 19

⇒ **Father** − **Son** = 19

The difference between the ages of two people remains **constant** throughout their lives.

Since the question asks for the difference between their present ages, it is directly obtained from the first equation.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fd0fd3f712631713262e86bdccb47b5bacaf3e24ca04701ded37192b3917a028.png] 

Let the present age of the **Father** be F and the **Son** be S.

**Case 1:** Sum of ages is 19 more than twice the son's age.

⇒ F + S = 2S + 19

⇒ F − S = 19 .................(1)

**Case 2:** After 15 years, 12 times father's age is 17 less than 13 times son's age.

⇒ 12(F + 15) = 13(S + 15) − 17

⇒ 12F + 180 = 13S + 195 − 17

⇒ 12F − 13S = 195 − 17 − 180

⇒ 12F − 13S = −2 .................(2)

From (1), F = S + 19. Substitute in (2):

⇒ 12(S + 19) − 13S = −2

⇒ 12S + 228 − 13S = −2

⇒ −S = −230 ⇒ S = 230 (This verifies the second condition holds for specific values, but the difference is already established).

⇒ Difference = F − S = 19 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two individuals never changes with time. If the difference is **x years** today, it will remain **x years** after **n years**.

questions.question: 3 years ago from now, the age of father was 30 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **age of son** 3 years ago be x.

**Father's age** then = 2x + 30.

Age difference = (2x + 30) − x = x + 30.

Difference in ages remains **constant** throughout life.

When father is twice the son's age, the difference (x + 30) must equal the **son's age** then.

Son's age then = x + 30. Current age of son = x + 3. Years from now = (x + 30) − (x + 3) = 27.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 3 years ago, Father's age = 2 × Son's age + 30.

**Formula:** Age difference is constant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e91d026f9f4b479b8f461f9bc3bbb468bd5776198ec33734a3df31ecc33645b.png] 

⇒ Let **Son's age** 3 years ago = S−₃ and **Father's age** = F−₃.

⇒ F−₃ = 2 × S−₃ + 30

⇒ **Age Difference** (D) = F−₃ − S−₃ = (2 × S−₃ + 30) − S−₃ = S−₃ + 30.

⇒ Let after **T years** from now, FT = 2 × ST.

⇒ Difference (D) = FT − ST = 2ST − ST = ST.

⇒ ST = S−₃ + 30.

⇒ Since ST is the age after T years from **present**, and S−₃ was age 3 years **before** present:

⇒ ST = Sₚᵣₑₛₑₙₜ + T = (S−₃ + 3) + T.

⇒ S−₃ + 30 = S−₃ + 3 + T.

⇒ T = 30 − 3 = 27.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people remains **constant** at any point in time.

When the age of one person is **n times** the age of another, the age difference is equal to (n−1) × the younger person's age.

Time Displacement

If current age is x, then age **'a' years ago** is (x − a) and age **'b' years later** is (x + b).</p

questions.question: 3 years ago from now, the age of father was 14 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?

questions.question: The sum of the age of A and 4 times the age of B is 37 years. When 7 times the age of A is added to 6 times the age of B, the result is 61 years. The sum of the ages (in years) of A and B is:

Let the ages of **A** and **B** be **A** and **B** years respectively.

Given: **A + 4B = 37** and **7A + 6B = 61**.

Multiply the first equation by 7: **7A + 28B = 259**.

Subtract the second equation from this: **(7A + 28B) − (7A + 6B) = 259 − 61** ⇒ **22B = 198** ⇒ **B = 9**.

Substitute **B = 9** in the first equation: **A + 4(9) = 37** ⇒ **A = 37 − 36 = 1**.

Sum of ages = **1 + 9 = 10**.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 years.**

⇒ Substitute in (2): **7(37 − 4B) + 6B = 61**

⇒ **259 − 28B + 6B = 61**

⇒ **259 − 22B = 61**

⇒ **22B = 198**

⇒ **B = 9**

⇒ Now, **A = 37 − 4(9) = 37 − 36 = 1**

⇒ Sum of ages = **A + B = 1 + 9 = 10**

**∴ The correct answer is 10 years.**

questions.question: If 5 times A's age is added to B's age, the sum is 95 years. If 2.2 times B's age is added to A's age, the sum is 63 years. What is B's age (in years)?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **A's age** be A and **B's age** be B.

From the first condition: 5A + B = 95 ⇒ B = 95 − 5A.

Substitute B in the second condition: A + 2.2(95 − 5A) = 63.

A + 209 − 11A = 63 ⇒ 10A = 146 ⇒ A = 14.6 years.

B = 95 − 5(14.6) = 95 − 73 = 22 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 22 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Condition 1: 5 × (A's age) + (B's age) = 95

Condition 2: (A's age) + 2.2 × (B's age) = 63

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f468f5eb4d7c64cc3eadbcf8e4e31f93af461a04c468c0ac6af95e19aff11958.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let A's age be A and B's age be B.

⇒ 5A + B = 95 → (i)

⇒ A + 2.2B = 63 → (ii)

Multiply equation (ii) by 5 to eliminate A:

⇒ 5(A + 2.2B) = 5 × 63

⇒ 5A + 11B = 315 → (iii)

Subtract equation (i) from equation (iii):

⇒ (5A + 11B) − (5A + B) = 315 − 95

⇒ 10B = 220

⇒ B = 220 ÷ 10

⇒ B = 22

**∴ The correct answer is 22 years.**

questions.question: {If } sin⁴theta - cos⁴theta = (1)/(2), { find the value of } 2sin²theta - 1.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given **sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ = 1/2**.

Using **a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)**, we get (sin²θ − cos²θ)(sin²θ + cos²θ) = 1/2.

Since **sin²θ + cos²θ = 1**, the expression becomes **sin²θ − cos²θ = 1/2**.

We know that **cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ**, so sin²θ − (1 − sin²θ) = **2sin²θ − 1 = 1/2**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0fd49775feb3e49562a6c6bfd688289a2f158cc3ba5f2bbc68dcfe0784de487e.png] 

**Given:** sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ = 1/2

**Formula Used:** a⁴ − b⁴ = (a² − b²)(a² + b²) and sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

⇒ (sin²θ)² − (cos²θ)² = 1/2

⇒ (sin²θ − cos²θ)(sin²θ + cos²θ) = 1/2

⇒ (sin²θ − cos²θ) × 1 = 1/2

⇒ sin²θ − (1 − sin²θ) = 1/2

⇒ sin²θ − 1 + sin²θ = 1/2

⇒ 2sin²θ − 1 = 1/2

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: The sum of 2 times Priya's present age and Jaya's present age is 48 years. Sanjay's is presently 2 times as old as Jaya. Mohit's present age is 4 years more than Priya's present age. The sum of the present ages of Sanjay and Mohit is 46 years. What is the sum of the present ages (in years) of Priya and Jaya?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Priya** = P, **Jaya** = J, **Sanjay** = S, **Mohit** = M.

Given: 2P + J = 48 and S + M = 46.

From conditions: S = 2J and M = P + 4.

Substitute in second equation: 2J + P + 4 = 46 ⇒ P + 2J = 42.

Solving 2P + J = 48 and P + 2J = 42 simultaneously ⇒ (2P + J) + (P + 2J) = 48 + 42 ⇒ 3(P + J) = 90 ⇒ P + J = 30.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ce2b17ea0b2103e6cad817463145b6ac3c121afa7f40cc6250eacdeba7a6b2e3.png] 

**Given:**

1) 2 × **Priya** (P) + **Jaya** (J) = 48

2) **Sanjay** (S) = 2 × **Jaya** (J)

3) **Mohit** (M) = **Priya** (P) + 4

4) **Sanjay** (S) + **Mohit** (M) = 46

**Calculations:**

⇒ Substitute (2) and (3) in (4): 2J + (P + 4) = 46

⇒ P + 2J = 42 −−− (Eq. A)

⇒ From (1): 2P + J = 48 −−− (Eq. B)

⇒ Adding (Eq. A) and (Eq. B): (P + 2J) + (2P + J) = 42 + 48

⇒ 3P + 3J = 90

⇒ 3(P + J) = 90

⇒ P + J = 90 ÷ 3 = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

If the sum (S) and difference (D) of two ages are known, the individual ages are (S+D)/2 and (S−D)/2.</p

Put **θ = 45°** to check options quickly.

Expression = (1/√2) × (1/√2) × (−1/√2) = −1/(2√2)

⇒ [sin²θ × cos²θ × (−cos²θ)] / [cosθ × sinθ × sinθ]

⇒ − (sin²θ × cos⁴θ) / (sin²θ × cosθ)

⇒ −cos³θ

questions.question: A person standing 30 metres away from a tower observes the angle of elevation to the top of the tower as 30°. Find the height of the tower.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **30°−60°−90°** right-angled triangle, the ratio of sides opposite to these angles is **1 : √3 : 2**.

Here, the side adjacent to 30° (base) corresponds to √3 units and the side opposite to 30° (height) corresponds to 1 unit.

√3 units = 30 m

1 unit = 30 ÷ √3 = (10 × 3) ÷ √3 = 10√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 10√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Distance from tower (Base) = 30 m, Angle of elevation (θ) = 30°.

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular (Height) ÷ Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/191063821f92455928ef86b14fd28c4c7e244879005d1f241b5441baff4591d9.png] 

⇒ tan 30° = Height ÷ 30

⇒ 1/√3 = Height ÷ 30

⇒ Height = 30 ÷ √3

⇒ Height = (30 × √3) ÷ (√3 × √3)

⇒ Height = 30√3 ÷ 3 = 10√3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 10√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

Standard values for tan are tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Angle of Elevation vs Depression

The **angle of elevation** is the angle between the horizontal line and the line of sight when looking up. The **angle of depression** is the same angle when looking down from the top.</p
